prompt: In three sentences, explain why the sky is blue.
content: The sky is blue because of Rayleigh scattering: sunlight is made up of all colors, and when it enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules. Shorter wavelengths of light (blue and violet) scatter much more strongly than longer wavelengths (like red and orange), so blue light gets bounced around the sky in all directions. Although violet light scatters even more, our eyes are less sensitive to violet and the sun emits less of it, so we perceive the sky as blue.
